author: ohtadmin
title: Tree board wants say on Ft. Getty plan
text:
The vice chairman of the tree committee said his board would like to have a say in the potential plantings that could accommodate the proposed plan to improve Fort Getty.
Richard Kingsley submitted his correspondence Dec. 31 to the ad hoc committee empaneled to explore the future of the 45-acre municipally owned park.
The letter, addressed to the committee’s chairwoman, Marisa Quinn, was copied to the project’s landscape architect, Arek Galle, who discussed potential trees during a Jan. 13 presentation to the committee.
“We are of the consensus that the central area needs improvement with plantings of shrubs or trees,” Kingsley wrote. “The present walking trails could be improved with plantings that are less invasive and more natural or native.”
Kingsley also said the trails “could also be improved, possibly with signage, through education in the areas of identification, history, wildlife and climate” with an emphasis on carbon sequestration of plants and trees.
Kingsley said the tree committee possibly could collaborate with the conservation commission to collect the information.
The letter also asked the ad hoc committee to consider creating more “primitive” and “wilderness-type” corridors while possibly creating a “mini-forest” in the park.
“The planting of more trees other than Eastern red cedar would be ideal,” Kingsley wrote. “We on the tree committee can help by suggesting species, placing and possibly maintenance of the plantings. Tree planting could also be an educational experience for adults and children.”
